He has skipped the last three Sundays without calling ahead.

It is his sister Marina, calling to remind him of the family's weekly Sunday lunch at their mother's house. She says they have missed him the past three weeks and asks if he is coming this time. He genuinely likes them, but the gatherings are loud, and with his hearing loss he often ends up nodding at jokes he did not catch. He is not wearing his hearing aids, because they irritate him when he is concentrating. The buzz of the phone brings back the last Sunday lunch he attended, when his nephew kept shouting a joke and he had to smile without understanding it. Marina's hopeful tone reminds him of the time she brought him a cake from their mother's kitchen and held it up so he could read her lips.
